It's really common for coping strategies to feel less effective during high-pressure moments, even when they help day-to-day. When deep breathing isn't cutting it during tests, try grounding techniques like the 5-4-3-2-1 method (noticing five things you see, four you hear, three you feel, two you smell, one you taste) to bring your attention back to the present. You might also try progressive muscle relaxation — briefly tensing and releasing your shoulders or hands can help discharge tension. Positive self-talk, like reminding yourself "I've prepared for this" or "This feeling will pass," can also help counter the spiral.

It could also be worth exploring whether your school offers accommodations for test anxiety, like extended time or a quieter testing environment. And if anxiety is interfering with your daily life and big moments consistently, talking to a counselor or mental health professional could help you build a broader toolkit. You deserve support that works when you need it most.
